text.en: Raju's mother pressed the mixer button and the motor hummed. "Electric power at work," said his father.

Electric current is the rate of flow of charge, I = Q / t, with the unit ampere. Potential difference between two points is the work done in moving a unit positive charge from one point to the other, and its unit is the volt. A working circuit needs a source and a complete conducting path. A switch controls the path, a bulb can act as a load, and meters are used to take measurements.
Ohm's law says that at constant temperature V = IR, where R is the resistance in ohms. For a uniform conductor, resistivity equals resistance times cross-sectional area divided by length. Conductance is the reciprocal of resistance. In series R = R1 + R2 + R3, and in parallel 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3.
Joule's law gives the heat produced as H = I^2 R t, used in heaters and bulbs. Electric power is P = VI with the unit watt, and electrical energy is measured in kilowatt hour. Domestic circuits use fuses and earthing, because overloading and short circuits cause danger.
Electric current is the rate of flow of charge, I = Q / t, with the unit ampere.
Potential difference between two points is the work done in moving a unit positive charge from one point to the other, and its unit is the volt.
A working circuit needs an energy source, conducting connections and a complete path. A switch can open the path. A bulb can be the load, and meters are added when measurements are needed.
Ohm's law says that at constant temperature V = IR, where R is the resistance in ohms.
Resistivity is a property of a material. For a uniform conductor it equals resistance times cross-sectional area divided by length. Conductance is the reciprocal of resistance.
In series R = R1 + R2 + R3, and in parallel 1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3.
Joule's law gives the heat produced as H = I^2 R t, used in heaters and bulbs.
Electric power is P = VI with the unit watt, and electrical energy is measured in kilowatt hour.
If twelve coulombs pass in three seconds, the average current is four amperes. One ampere means one coulomb per second.
In a metallic wire the electrons drift the other way. Circuit arrows generally show the direction of conventional current.

board.text: Conventional current goes from positive to negative outside the cell

text.en: A potential difference of six volts transfers six joules of energy per coulomb of charge passing through a component.

board.text: One volt means one joule per coulomb

text.en: Place an ammeter in the path whose current you want to measure. The same branch current flows through both the meter and the component.
Connect the voltmeter across the component to compare electric potential at its two ends.
Keep the temperature steady. If doubling the voltage doubles the current, the voltage divided by current stays constant.

board.text: Ohmic conductor: voltage rises in proportion to current

text.en: If six volts cause two amperes through a resistor, the resistance is three ohms.
Put current on the horizontal axis and voltage on the vertical axis. For an ohmic conductor the straight graph’s slope gives resistance.

board.text: Read V against I on a graph

text.en: For identical material and thickness, a longer wire has larger resistance. With twice the length, there is twice the resistance at the same temperature.
A wire of twice the cross-sectional area has half the resistance when its material, length and temperature stay fixed.
There is only one route through resistors in series. The individual voltage drops add to the supply voltage.

board.text: Series components carry the same current

text.en: A resistor added in series increases the total opposition to current. Add the resistance values directly.

board.text: Series: 6 Ω plus 3 Ω makes 9 Ω

text.en: Both ends of each branch are connected to the same pair of nodes. Each branch therefore gets the same potential difference.

board.text: Parallel branches have the same voltage

text.en: Across six volts, a six-ohm resistor draws one ampere and a three-ohm resistor draws two. The supply current is three amperes.

board.text: Add branch currents at a junction

text.en: Divide the six-volt supply by the total current of three amperes. The pair of branches acts like a single two-ohm resistor.

board.text: Equivalent parallel resistance is smaller than either branch

text.en: For a constant current in a resistor, doubling the current produces four times the heat over the same time, if resistance stays the same.
At six volts and two amperes, the power is twelve watts. The circuit transfers twelve joules per second to the component.

board.text: Power is the rate of energy transfer

text.en: A one-kilowatt appliance used for half an hour uses half a kilowatt-hour. Kilowatt measures power and kilowatt-hour measures energy.
Appliances receive the supply voltage across their branches and can be switched independently. Learn with diagrams or supervised low-voltage equipment.

board.text: Household loads are connected in parallel

text.en: Overload can occur when too many loads draw current together. A safety device opens the circuit if the current becomes excessive.

board.text: A short circuit gives current an unintended low-resistance route

text.en: An earth connection helps protective devices disconnect a faulty appliance if a live wire touches its metal case.
LEDs use semiconductor materials and commonly use less electric power than older filament lamps for similar lighting.

board.text: An LED turns electrical energy into light

problem.en: A 4 ohm and a 6 ohm resistor are in series. Find the total resistance.

text.en: In series, add resistances.
Total R = 10 ohm.

problem.en: Find the current if 15 C passes through a wire in 5 seconds.

text.en: Use I = Q/t = 15/5.

why.en: Current measures charge passing per second.

text.en: The average current is 3 A.

why.en: Each second carries an average of 3 coulombs.

problem.en: Find the equivalent resistance of 6 Ω and 3 Ω in parallel at 6 V.

text.en: Branch currents are 6/6 = 1 A and 6/3 = 2 A.

why.en: Both branches have 6 V across them.

text.en: The current sums to 3 A, so R = 6/3 = 2 Ω.

why.en: The equivalent resistor draws the same total current.

problem.en: How much energy does a 2 kW appliance use in 15 minutes?

text.en: Convert 15 minutes to 0.25 h.

why.en: Kilowatt-hours use power in kilowatts and time in hours.

text.en: Energy = 2 × 0.25 = 0.50 kWh.

why.en: Use power multiplied by elapsed time.

prompt.en: A friend says In parallel, the total resistance is more than the largest resistor. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: In parallel total resistance is less than the smallest.
